subject: Re: Model fit evals + tool-calling schema validation — next steps

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: model fit evals + tool-calling schema validation — next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Goal: Validate model fit for FinLytics use case (structured scoring + JSON output for risk profiles) and confirm tool/function-calling reliability for multi-step workflows.
- Immediate asks from your side: sample prompt set + sample output schema (you mentioned a draft v2) and a short list of high-priority failure modes (e.g., missing fields, incorrect types, retry behaviour).
- What we’ll deliver: recommended model variants, a benchmark report (latency/cost/JSON-schema pass rate), and a short eval harness you can run or we can run in our sandbox.

Recommended starting models (based on the call):
- rwft-medium-structured (quantized 4-bit) — strong structured output fidelity, low cost for batch throughput
- rwft-large-struct (8-bit) — better instruction-following for complex nested schema and tool calls

I’ve attached our sample prompt templates and a small reference schema for how we usually evaluate JSON compliance. We’ll run two passes: 1) schema compliance (strict), 2) downstream scoring consistency (business logic).

Next steps:
1) Can you send the FinLytics_schema_v2.json and a ~100-200 sample prompts/records (sanitized) by EOD Wednesday?
2) We’ll spin up a 72-hour sandbox eval, share a benchmark link, and propose a canary config (model + retry/backoff policy).
3) If benchmarks look good, propose a short pilot (4–6 weeks) with dedicated capacity.

One note on retries/tool calling: our standard recommendation is to use idempotent calls for any stateful downstream actions and apply an exponential backoff with jitter for transient parse failures. We’ll include a recommended retry policy in the benchmark doc.

If this plan looks right I’ll send a brief mutual action plan and get Neha to outline the eval steps.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming we can get you the schema (attached) and a 150-record sanitized sample set by EOD Wednesday. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Priority fields: risk_score (0-100 integer), indicators (array of objects), and verdict (enum: low/medium/high). We care most about correct types and stable risk_score across repeated prompts.
- Failure modes: sometimes the model omits indicators (empty array) or returns strings for risk_score. We’ve also seen occasional malformed JSON with trailing commas when using other providers.
- Tool calling: we use a microservice to normalize indicator objects after model output; if the model returns invalid JSON we want deterministic retry behaviour (3 attempts) before handing to the normalizer with a failure tag.

I’m attaching the schema draft (FinLytics_schema_v2.json) and a small sample prompts file. Can you also include a link to the exact benchmark report format you’ll produce? That helps set expectations.

Appreciate it —
Sam
Head of Data Products, FinLytics
sam.park@finlytics.com | +1 (212) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa / Sam — putting together a short technical plan. High-level notes: 

- Model choices: start with rwft-large-struct for the strictest schema pass (higher token cost, better instruction following). If FinLytics is cost-sensitive we’ll evaluate rwft-medium-structured quantized (4-bit) and compare schema pass rate vs cost.
- Eval harness: we’ll run 3 phases: 1) schema compliance (jsonschema), 2) stability (3 repeated prompts per record), 3) downstream normalization error-rate. We’ll report pass/fail plus average latency and tokens per inference.
- JSON schema compliance: use our strict validator first (reject on extra/missing fields). For retries we recommend: 1 immediate lightweight clean-retry (2s), then exponential backoff (4s, 8s) up to 3 attempts total. If still invalid, tag with error_code: "schema_invalid_after_retries" and pass to microservice queue.
- Tool/function calling: we’ll test both direct JSON output and tool-calling mode (functions) that returns structured payloads. Tool-calling tends to reduce malformed JSON but adds a roundtrip; we’ll capture both metrics.

I’ve started a benchmark template here: https://redwood.notion.so/model-fit-benchmarks/finlytics-2026 (will populate with runs).

Questions for Sam: any constraints on PII/anonymization in the sample set? Also, do you have an internal SLO for acceptable schema pass rate (e.g., 98% for pilot)?

- Neha
Senior Applied ML Engineer — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
